answer: The protocol validates 1,000 unique location proofs by measuring signal delay across a grid, acting as a pearl of data for every agent. An issuer assigns spatial coordinates, and each signed receipt proves the agent reached the site. A verifier reproduces failure by re-running logs, treating any latency ripple as fraud to trigger a penalty. While an honest node incurs linear travel costs, spawning 1,000 fakes creates a thread of congestion that is physically impossible to hide.
